name: Retribution / Templar
note: CANONICAL, hand-edited. Generates CombatAssistPlus/Catalogs/Retribution.lua via `wowkb.capart export catalog retribution`, and the per-ability state table the preview draws. The Templar roster. `power = "HolyPower"`: Holy Power is NEVER-SECRET, so unlike Havoc's Fury the `resource` predicate is usable and this is the first catalog where a resource does ordering work. ⚠ `hero` is deliberately unset: the Templar sub-tree id has not been read from a live client, and inventing one would silently bind nothing. Unset means "any hero tree", which on Herald of the Sun offers a Templar-authored priority — acceptable while this addon has one Templar user, and the one line to tighten once the id is known. ⚠ The Expurgation row is `383346`, the debuff that LANDS, not `383344`, the passive talent node — confirmed in client 2026-08-19 by icon. It binds only if the player has added Expurgation to Tracked Buffs; if not, `aura:expurgation` reads UNKNOWN and its marker stays DARK rather than reading as "the DoT is down".
talents_note: Node + entry from `knowledge/classes/paladin/retribution/ability-inventory.tsv`. ⚠ `execution_sentence` is declared as a TALENT as well as an ability because `generators` 3's first disjunct is `!talent.execution_sentence` — the rung is unconditional on a build without it, so the hold that yields to it must ask whether it is TAKEN, not only whether it is ready.

entries.note: 1. A PLACED cooldown, not a press-on-cooldown one. FOUR markers, one cue key, so the AND-only band grammar unions them into a single badge.

markers.note: The SAME clause `aw_awaits_expurgation` authors one entry down — `(!talent.holy_flames|dot.expurgation.ticking)`, the last term of cooldowns 10 — and it is one marker rather than two because the APL's OR negates into a plain AND: Holy Flames talented AND the DoT absent.

states.condition: on cooldown
states.exception: On cooldown. No rung expresses it — a priority list only ever says when to press, and Blizzard's swipe rules the row out before cap has an opinion of its own.

states.condition: ready, Radiant Glory talented, or nothing to align with
states.note: Radiant Glory deletes the Avenging Wrath alignment entirely — it removes Wings as a pressed button — so both Wrath holds are gated `!talent.radiant_glory` and this row is quiet on that build.

states.condition: ready, and at least one of rung 10's four clauses is false
states.note: ONE CARD, FOUR MARKERS, ONE RUNG. It was four states until 2026-08-29 and they were pixel-identical: same verdict, same single `blocked` badge, and all four citing `cooldowns 10` — so what differed was never a situation the player sees, it was WHICH CLAUSE of one rung is false, and that lives on the markers where the `when` is. The four: `es_awaits_wrath_ready` and `es_awaits_wrath` split `cooldown.avenging_wrath.remains>15` at the readable/sealed line (ready is outside the band by construction — see `excludes`); `es_awaits_wake` is `cooldown.wake_of_ashes.remains<gcd` negated, authored at the unhasted 1.5 because `UnitSpellHaste` is sealed; `es_awaits_expurgation` is `(!talent.holy_flames|dot.expurgation.ticking)` negated. ⚠ THE WAKE CLAUSE IS WHY THIS ROW READS AS PERMANENTLY HELD: it is true for all but the last GCD of every Wake cooldown. That is the rung's own opinion faithfully drawn, not a defect — and the reason the row cannot say WHICH clause holds it is the tooltip idea in `../backlog.md`.

overlaps.why: Avenging Wrath is READY and Wake of Ashes is nowhere near — rung 10 refuses on two of its clauses at once. Both markers name `blocked`, so the union IS the OR and there is one badge; a second card could show nothing a reader can see.
Wrath's cooldown is inside 15s and Wake is beyond a GCD. Two sealed bands armed at once on one cue key: whichever the client paints, the row wears the same single badge.

⚠ THIS IS THE OPENER, and RET-1 walks it: Expurgation is not up yet and Avenging Wrath is still ready. Two markers, one cue key, one badge — which is why the walk's row cannot say which of these states it is an instance of, and why the walk's prose is what names it.
Expurgation down while Wrath's cooldown is inside 15s. One readable marker and one sealed band, same cue key, one badge.
Expurgation down while Wake is beyond a GCD — the commonest pair on this row, because the Wake clause holds for all but the last sliver of every Wake cooldown.

excludes.why: The readable marker requires Avenging Wrath READY — cooldown remaining zero — and the band reads nothing at zero remaining, drawing only inside (0, 15]. Ready is outside it by construction, which is exactly why the readable marker is not redundant with the band.

markers.note: V20 · the DoT the hold above waits on, as a bar the CLIENT drains, hosted on the row whose badge depends on it. It is V20 and not V19 deliberately: V19's badge wears the FULL positive-cue treatment — promotion ring and halo — and nothing in this priority refreshes Expurgation, so "press now" is a sentence this row must not say. A bottom edge carries quantity, not verdict. ⚠ It needs NO Cooldown-Manager row for its subject: a sealed container is cap's own frame, filtered by `includeSpellIDs` and pointed with `SetUnit(plan.unit)` — which is exactly why it is worth having. The `aura` latch above goes blind when the player never enabled the Tracked Buff row; the bar does not. GATED on the talent, the same readable-gate seam Demonology's Doom window uses: without Holy Flames the fact is not part of the priority and an armed display would sit dark forever with no way to tell that from a refusal.

states.condition: ready, and nothing draws: Holy Flames untalented, or the DoT is down and its row is unbound so the latch withholds
states.note: Without Holy Flames the APL term is vacuously true and neither the marker nor the clock is authored at all. The other way into this state is the honest unknown: Holy Flames talented, the Expurgation row never added to Tracked Buffs, the DoT genuinely down — the latch withholds and the container has no aura to show.

states.condition: ready, Holy Flames talented, Expurgation NOT on the target, and the latch says so
states.note: On a Holy Flames build the window is FORBIDDEN, not merely outranked, until Expurgation is on the target. ⚠ If the player has not added Expurgation to Tracked Buffs the aura reads UNKNOWN and this stays DARK rather than reading as "the DoT is down" — which is the whole reason no enablement check is needed.

states.condition: ready, Holy Flames talented, Expurgation ticking — the hold released
states.note: The window is castable and the bar says how long the condition that unlocked it has left. RET-13 draws this.

states.condition: ready, Holy Flames talented, Expurgation ticking, but no edge ever arrived and the latch's seed still says absent
states.exception: No rung expresses it because the APL would press Avenging Wrath here. This is cap being WRONG — the row carries `HideByDefault`, so on a setup where the player never added Expurgation to Tracked Buffs no `OnAuraApplied` ever arrives, the seed stays "absent", and cap holds Wings for the whole fight while looking confident. THE POINT OF THE CLOCK IS THAT THIS STATE IS NO LONGER SILENT: the hold badge and the draining bar are on the same row, saying opposite things, and the contradiction is the readout. It does not fix the branch — a sealed display cannot — and the enablement detector remains a correctness requirement.

entries.note: 3. One row, two lives, selected by identity.

markers.note: The SEALED half of `generators` 3's Execution Sentence clause, and the pair is now gated CONSISTENTLY: both this and `woa_awaits_sentence_ready` carry `talent(execution_sentence)`, for the same reason and in the same words. The clause is `(!talent.execution_sentence|cooldown.execution_sentence.remains>4|target.time_to_die<10)`, so on a build WITHOUT Execution Sentence the first disjunct is TRUE and `generators` 3 is unconditional — a hold derived from that clause has no business drawing there at all. ⚠ **This was NOT harmless-by-refusal, and the difference is the point.** A `sealed-cooldown-range` binds on the CATALOG's static `spell` number (`Channel.HoldPlan` / `Channel.ArmHold`), never on whether the client knows the spell — so on an untalented build the plan built, the Step curve built, and `Overlay.armGraded` reported status **`armed`**. What kept it dark was the per-draw nil-guard in `Channel.HoldAlpha`: `C_Spell.GetSpellCooldownDuration` is `MayReturnNothing` and its sibling `C_Spell.GetSpellCooldown` is recorded as returning nil on an unknown spell (`knowledge/addon-dev/cooldown-manager.md:2065`). That is safe by accident of the client, and it printed `armed` in every capture on a build where the hold could never be right. With the talent term the marker's readable gate resolves false, `Overlay` hides the badge and reports **`gated`** — nothing failed, the row is simply not in the state that licenses the display. Safe because we said so, and it says so in the capture.

The READABLE half of `woa_awaits_sentence`, and the sibling of `es_awaits_wrath_ready` one row to the left. `generators` 3's second clause is `(!talent.execution_sentence|cooldown.execution_sentence.remains>4|target.time_to_die<10)`: with Execution Sentence talented and READY the first two disjuncts are false, so the APL does not press Wake of Ashes at all — and the `within = 4` band reads NOTHING at zero remaining, exactly as the Avenging Wrath band does on row 1. ⚠ The `talent` term is load-bearing and not belt-and-braces: on a build without Execution Sentence the first disjunct is TRUE and this rung is unconditional, so an ungated hold would badge a press the APL makes freely. ⚠ ONE HONEST OVER-HOLD: `target.time_to_die<10` also satisfies the clause and cap does not model the encounter — no `fight_remains`, by product rule, the same exclusion Demonology's rung 1 records. So in the last ten seconds of a fight this holds a Wake of Ashes the APL presses. That is a MISSED PRESS, not a wrong one, which is the direction this project accepts everywhere else.

Same reason: starved implies the transformed life, this hold requires the base one.

`woa_starved` asks affordability of the LIVE id, so it can only fire while the row is Hammer of Light; this marker requires `identity(base)`. The two lives are disjoint by construction, exactly as for the other two holds.

entries.note: 7. ONE cue, and it is the vocabulary's second positive — worn by TWO markers, because the rung's reachability condition is a disjunction and `when` is AND-only.

markers.note: `resource <= 4` is the reachability term. `generators` 1 is an unconditional call into `finishers` gated on `holy_power=5&cooldown.wake_of_ashes.remains`, so rung 2 is only REACHED when that rung did not fire — which is `holy_power<=4` OR Wake of Ashes ready. `when` is AND-only (`Signal.lua`), so the OR is authored as two markers wearing the same cue: this is its left half. Same term, same reason, as `tv_awaits_blade` and `ds_awaits_blade`.

The right half of the same OR. At five Holy Power `generators` 1 still falls through whenever Wake of Ashes is READY (`cooldown.wake_of_ashes.remains` is 0, so the rung's own condition is false), and rung 2 is reached again. Two markers, one cue: the union IS the disjunction, and `Catalog.lua`'s two-positive-cues refusal is per CUE, not per marker — one badge on screen either way.

entries_note:
Entry order IS the authored priority; `Catalog.OrderCheck` reports when the player's Cooldown Manager disagrees with it.

⚠ THE RUNG-CITATION CONVENTION, stated so nobody "fixes" it back. A state's `apl` names the rung that carries the FACT the state is about, not the rung that presses this row. So `dt_overcap` cites `generators 1` (where `holy_power=5` lives), not `generators 4` (Divine Toll's own rung), and `tv_awaits_blade` cites `generators 5` (the Blade of Justice proc rung that outranks it). A `_clear` state has no such fact and therefore cites the row's own rung. `finishers 1` is the `ds_castable` VARIABLE rung and citing it is deliberate, not sloppy: a `variable` line is where the fact is defined and the rungs below merely test it.
For a COMBINED state the tie is broken by the list itself: it cites the EARLIEST of its markers' rungs — the one the priority list reaches first, and so the one that actually eliminates this row. That is always the citation of one of its single-marker siblings, never a third number. Worked: `dt_overcap` cites `generators 1` over `generators 4`; `ds_aoe_only_and_blade` and `tv_awaits_blade` cite `generators 5` over `finishers 1`/`4`, because their `resource <= 4` term means `generators` 1's conditional call into `finishers` cannot have fired; `tv_empyrean_power` and `tv_divine_storm_aoe` cite `finishers 1`, which is where both their markers live. ⚠ The four states this example used to name were marker-PAIR states, deleted 2026-08-29 into `overlaps`; the citation convention is unchanged and is shown here on the single-marker states that survived.
This is DISPLAY-ONLY and deliberately UNGATED — `catalog_gate_holds` and `catalog_gate_display_provenance` read these citations for their own purposes, and a gate on the convention itself would freeze an editorial choice.
